issues.description: The problem statement and UML describe a shared inventory class named 'Stock' (and instruct students to use a static stock attribute of type Stock). However, the provided starter code defines and exposes a class named Inventory (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java) and the reference solution's SealSaloon uses a static field of type Inventory (SealSaloon: private static final Inventory stock = new Inventory()). At the same time src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java in the template is empty. This mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) creates ambiguity for students: should they implement/modify a class named Stock as the spec says, or work with the existing Inventory class in the template? It can lead to compilation errors or incorrect implementations if students follow the UML but the template and solution use Inventory.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the inventory class name consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred): update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' (not 'Stock') and clarify that the static stock attribute should be of type Inventory. Remove or document the empty src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java file. Option B: rename the Inventory class and file to Stock everywhere (template, solution, tests) and update references accordingly. Ensure the class name used in the UML, problem description, starter files, and solution match exactly so students know which class to use.
